transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Pioneer Health), Samir Khan (Head of Security), Priya Nair (Platform Engineer)

Summary: High-level security intake to evaluate options between Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Primary concerns: SSO/SAML integration (Okta/AzureAD), KMS key ownership/rotation (bring-your-own-key vs managed), audit logs and retention, data residency and retention/purge policies, and initial benchmarking for latency/cost.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 compliance artifacts, SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning, RBAC model (least privilege, tenant separation), audit log format and retention windows, encryption at rest & in transit (customer keys, HSM), VPC peering and network egress, data retention/purge requests and legal holds.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine (AE): Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we wanted to focus this call on the security intake and make sure we capture any blockers for you moving forward. Marcus is our SE, he'll dive into the tech bits.
[00:14] Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO): Yeah thanks. We want to understand: can we run the models in a way that keeps PHI isolated and ensures we meet our SOC2 and ISO efforts. We're also evaluating a couple of other vendors so the security ask is high priority.
[00:29] Marcus (SE): Great, Elena. High-level — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. For PHI workloads most customers are looking at Dedicated or Private. We do SOC 2, and can share ISO summary — quick q, Samir: are you more concerned about key ownership or network isolation?
[00:42] Samir (Head of Security): Honestly both. Key ownership is big — we need BYOK, key rotation logs, HSM-backed KMS, and an auditable rotation schedule. Network-wise we prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress.
[00:55] Priya (Platform): And from infra ops we need the exact peering steps, IP ranges, and whether Redwood requires proxying for model updates or if models can be staged via a bucket inside our VPC.
[01:08] Marcus (SE): Right. For BYOK we support customer-managed KMS — you can bring an AWS KMS key or a managed HSM. Rotation events are logged and we can push logs to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail. There is also envelope encryption on the payloads.
[01:22] Dr. Elena: When you say logs, are those full request payloads or just metadata? We can't have any raw PHI in your logs.
[01:31] Marcus: Good point. By default payloads are not stored in plaintext in audit logs; logs include request id, model, token counts, latency, but sensitive fields can be redacted. For hosted we have a longer retention for analytics; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and opt out of store.
[01:49] Samir: Can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted API ever decrypts customer-managed keys inside Redwood? That is, do keys leave our control?
[01:58] Marcus: If you provide BYOK via a customer-managed AWS KMS key in your account, decryption happens in your account's HSM and tokens are encrypted crossing the boundary. For hosted patterns we use a secure envelope approach where Redwood holds only wrapped keys; unwrapping requires KMS call in your account. Note: older transcripts and doc examples sometimes show 'K-V cash' in voice parsers — ignore that.
[02:20] Jasmine: We should also clarify SSO SAML flow — Samir, you're using Okta?
[02:25] Samir: Yes Okta + AzureAD for partners. We want SAML 2.0 support, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC syncing with our groups. Minimum requirement: SSO with enforced MFA and team-level roles.
[02:37] Marcus: Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; Okta and Azure AD are common. We also offer SCIM for user provisioning and attribute mapping. Role sync is plumbable into RBAC so you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles — and you can define custom roles for least privilege.
[02:52] Priya: If someone is deprovisioned in Okta, how fast does Redwood revoke access?
[02:57] Marcus: SCIM push is near-real-time, usually under a minute for user disable events. For active tokens, we can force token invalidation on deprovision but need to coordinate session TTLs.
[03:10] Dr. Elena: For audit/a11y we need immutable audit logs that satisfy our internal compliance team — can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[03:19] Marcus: Yes — logs can stream to your SIEM via our log forwarder or to CloudWatch/CloudTrail in your account (for Dedicated/Private). Hosted customers can request log forwarding as part of an enterprise add-on.
[03:31] Samir: What about change history for model rollouts — we need to track who rolled which model and when, and be able to roll back.
[03:39] Jasmine: That's part of Redwood Console — per-route/model dashboards, audit entries for rollouts, canary decisions, A/Bs and rollbacks. We can include the audit trail in exports.
[03:50] Priya: On data residency: our data must not leave the EU for certain studies. Can you restrict regions and block failover to US?
[03:59] Marcus: Yes, you can pin region or model routing policy to EU-only infra. For Hosted we have region controls; Dedicated and Private give you total control over physical placement. Fallback policies can be disabled to avoid cross-region failover.
[04:13] Dr. Elena: Good. On retention: we need 30 days of raw logs, 7 years for certain audit artifacts, and ability to perform ad-hoc legal hold and export. Is that possible?
[04:23] Marcus: We support configurable retention per data type. Raw request storage is configurable (zero to X days). Audit artifacts can be set to longer archives; for long term retention we recommend configuring exports to your archival bucket. Legal holds are a workflow we support in Private/Dedicated where you can mark records to prevent purge.
[04:38] Samir: Encryption in transit? We require TLS 1.2+, mutual TLS for some backchannel ops.
[04:45] Marcus: TLS 1.2+ is enforced. Mutual TLS is available for certain peering endpoints and private control plane communications.
[04:53] Jasmine: Let's touch on RBAC model briefly — Marcus?
[04:56] Marcus: Redwood RBAC has pre-baked roles (admin, dev, viewer), and you can create custom roles with permission scoping to models, routes, or projects. Multi-tenant isolation is enforced in Dedicated; Private can be deployed in a tenant-isolated fashion on your network.
[05:12] Priya: Do you integrate with our existing vault or KMS for secrets (DB creds, S3 keys)?
[05:17] Marcus: Yes — we support external secret stores, Vault integrations, and referencing secrets stored in your KMS. We don't store raw secrets unless explicitly configured and encrypted.
[05:25] Samir: I want to call out compliance artifacts: can you provide your SOC 2 Type II report, and an ISO 27001 cert summary?
[05:33] Jasmine: Absolutely. We'll send the SOC 2 Type II summary and the ISO attestation. For hosted customers we provide redacted reports under NDA; for Dedicated/Private we can provide additional operational evidence.
[05:46] Dr. Elena: About model artifacts — if we upload custom models, who has access to the model weights, and are they encrypted at rest?
[05:55] Marcus: Any model artifacts you upload can be stored in your account (for Dedicated/Private) and encrypted at rest. For hosted, we have per-tenant storage options where models are encrypted; access is limited by RBAC and keys can be customer-managed. We do not train on customer uploads.
[06:12] Priya: Networking question — will we need to open inbound ports to Redwood or is it outbound only?
[06:18] Marcus: Mostly outbound from your side for API calls. For VPC peering there's path-based connectivity; if you choose private deployment we deploy inside your VPC and there will be internal endpoints.
[06:29] Samir: You mentioned audit log format earlier — JSONL, right?
[06:33] Marcus: Yes, logs are JSONL with event types, timestamps, actor, request id. We can include token counts and masked prompt hashes, not full prompt text unless you opt-in.
[06:45] Dr. Elena: Masked prompt hashes — we need determinism for deduping, but not reversible. Good.
[06:51] Marcus: Exactly.
[06:53] Jasmine: Are there any regulatory-specific controls you need us to call out — e.g., HIPAA BAA?
[06:59] Samir: We're not HIPAA-covered broadly, but some of our partner studies are. We would want to know if Redwood is willing to sign a BAA for Dedicated/Private.
[07:09] Marcus: We can discuss BAAs with legal; historically Dedicated/Private contracts include BAA options depending on scope.
[07:16] Priya: For the PoC, we plan to run a small inference workload with sample de-identified records to measure latency and cost. We need a benchmark template.
[07:25] Marcus: We'll share a benchmark template that includes tokenization pattern, sequence lengths, qps, and expected latencies across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We'll also provide recommended batching and quantization knobs.
[07:36] Dr. Elena: Cost vs latency — we need some anchor numbers. How do Dedicated slots compare to Hosted per-token?
[07:42] Jasmine: Quick note — pricing varies with commit and model size. Dedicated gives much more predictable unit cost at volume; Hosted is simple to start. We'll share sample pricing tiers in the follow up.
[07:53] Samir: Regarding data purge — if a user requests deletion, what's the SLA and can you guarantee deletion from backups?
[07:59] Marcus: Deletion from primary stores is immediate upon request; backups may have retention windows. For Dedicated/Private you control backup policies; for Hosted we can offer agreements to shorten backup retention for enterprise deals. We support data deletion exports for verification.
[08:16] Priya: Any known gotchas for Kubernetes-based private deployments? We run on k8s with strict Admission Controllers and limited host privileges.
[08:25] Marcus: Our on-prem package supports running under restricted k8s environments; we document required capabilities and have a hardened chart. We'll produce a checklist for Admission Controllers, PodSecurity, and necessary privileges.
[08:37] Dr. Elena: For the KMS rotation, can we get rotation logs pushed to our SIEM and have an audit of who requested rotation?
[08:45] Marcus: Yes — rotation events can be logged in CloudTrail and forwarded. We keep audit entries for key lifecycle events and operator actions.
[08:54] Samir: Are private keys ever backed up to Redwood's control plane?
[08:59] Marcus: No, with BYOK keys stay in your KMS/HSM; Redwood receives wrapped keys for operation but cannot unwrap without KMS permission.
[09:10] Jasmine: Quick check — any blockers to proceeding with a PoC? Samir?
[09:14] Samir: Need to see SOC2 and KMS rotation policy and clarify BAA approach. Also want the benchmark template and the Private deployment network checklist.
[09:26] Priya: From platform side, sample VPC peering steps and allowed egress ranges.
[09:32] Marcus: We'll prepare those. Also, I want to surface a potential perf note — for low-latency we suggest model variants with smaller context and prefix caching; that affects cost/latency tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[09:45] Dr. Elena: Fine. Also, what SLAs do you give for Dedicated?
[09:49] Jasmine: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers — 99.9% by default for latency/availability with options for higher depending on commit. We'll include SLA options in pricing doc.
[09:59] Samir: One more: encryption algorithm — what ciphers do you use for at-rest and in-transit?
[10:04] Marcus: At-rest we use AES-256-GCM for object stores and envelope encryption; in-transit TLS 1.2+/1.3 with modern ciphers. HSM-backed keys are FIPS validated in supported clouds.
[10:19] Priya: For SCIM, do you support group nesting mapping? Our org uses nested groups heavily.
[10:25] Marcus: We support nesting via group attribute expansion; mapping complexity can be handled in provisioning rules.
[10:33] Jasmine: Let's go into the wrap-up and next steps.
[10:36] Jasmine (AE): Recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO attestation & redacted report under NDA, PoC benchmark template, Private/Dedicated network checklist, and draft pricing/SLA. Pioneer to share KMS inventory and rotation policy.
[10:50] Dr. Elena: Sounds good. Can we target docs by Friday?
[10:54] Jasmine: We'll send SOC2 summary and pricing by 2026-11-14 and the longer pack by 2026-11-13. Marcus will send the benchmark template and network checklist by 2026-11-20.
[11:06] Samir: Great. One last question — monitoring and alerts: can Redwood push security alerts to our pager?
[11:12] Marcus: Yes alerting integrations to PagerDuty and Slack are supported — we can forward security incidents and operational warnings.
[11:20] Priya: Thanks all.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: SOC2 Type II (redacted), ISO attestation, benchmark template (to be provided), VPC peering and Private deploy checklist (to be provided), draft pricing tiers.

End of transcript.

Post-call recap (added by AE): Jasmine to create calendar invite for PoC kickoff (w/ Marcus and Pioneer infra team) tentatively week of 2026-11-23. NDA already in place; will attach redacted SOC2.
